messages.subject: mixedmirt (random intercept)
parts:
Hi Phil,

I experienced a hard time understanding what is working on behind mixedmirt. For simplicity, I simulated a random intercept data, where sample size 3000, group=200, using Rasch model, and the syntax is as follows:

~~~~~~
rm(list=ls())
set.seed(1234)
N <- 3000
a <- matrix(rep(1,10),10,1) # all ones
d <- matrix(seq(-2,2,length.out=10),10,1); d[1] = 0
cluster = 200
random_intercept = rnorm(cluster,0,1)
Theta = numeric()
for (i in 1:cluster){
    Theta <- c(Theta, rnorm(N/cluster,0,1) + random_intercept[i])
    }
group = factor(rep(paste0('G',1:cluster), each = N/cluster))
covdata <- data.frame(group)
data <- simdata(a,d,N, itemtype = rep('dich',10), Theta=matrix(Theta))
mod1 <- mixedmirt(data, covdata, 1, fixed = ~ 0 + items, random = ~ 1|group)
coef(mod1, printSE = TRUE)
~~~~~~

The item estimates were fine, but the variance of theta and variance of random intercept were not 1 and 1:

$GroupPars
    MEAN_1 COV_11
par      0  1.727
SE      NA    NaN

$group
    COV_group_group
par           0.156
SE              NaN

Not sure if I simulated incorrectly?

How to estimate the mean of random intercept? (and put constrain on item estimate, overall mean is zero)

Thank you~

Yes, but specific decomposition of the traits is not yet supported. One can get around this by including general intercept differences, but these will largely be agnostic to the multidimensional traits used (which has pros and cons). Ability decomposition support will be coming at a later time.
Or alternatively can mirt() allows for covariates (latent regression)?

Also yes, but does not support random effects (and probably never will). fscores() will also account for the latent structures in mirt(), allowing for plausible values and other related methods. Cheers.

Phil

Phil
